those secretory proteins in the liver that are altered in response 
to injury or infection, results in rapid loss of lean body 
mass and an increased net negative nitrogen balance, which 
continues until the inflammatory response resolves. Break-
down of protein tissue also causes increased urinary losses of 
potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium. Lipid metabolism 
also is altered in stress and sepsis. Increased circulation of free 
fatty acids is thought to result from increased lipolysis caused 
by elevated catecholamines and cortisol, as well as a marked 
elevation in the ratio of glucagon to insulin.
